A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToG-2 research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching despite the expanded appendix in v6.

before.justification: v4 reports original ToG-2 benchmark results, component and backbone ablations, runtime measurements, and manual analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and adds Creak case analysis, pruning-threshold experiments, incomplete-graph evaluations, runtime comparisons, and significance tests.

M1.justification: Section 3, Equations 1–7, Algorithm 1, and the appendix prompts retain the same retrieval and reasoning procedure. The newly specified pruning threshold documents existing low-score filtering. Revised call accounting includes query rewriting already described in v4.

E1.justification: The established QA, fact-verification, and Chinese financial QA coverage is retained. Appendix B.7 adds a distinct degraded-retrieval scenario: HotpotQA questions evaluated while retaining only 30%, 50%, or 80% of discovered graph entities and relations.

E2.justification: v4's runtime comparison evaluates ToG-2 against ToG. v6 adds CoK and NaiveRAG to the efficiency comparison in Table 9. The comparator sets in the main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported exploration temperature from 0.4 to 0, with reasoning remaining at 0; the PDFs do not establish that retained results were rerun. New protocols include a 50-example Creak audit, a three-threshold sweep, a 100-question graph-deletion experiment with alternative width/depth settings, and total-runtime/API-call comparisons.

E4.justification: v6 substantially expands analysis beyond the retained component, backbone, retrieval-tool, and self-consistency studies. It adds Creak answer-source analysis and three failure cases, relation-pruning threshold sensitivity, graph-incompleteness robustness with an exploration adjustment, and broader efficiency analysis in Appendix B.

E5.justification: v4 contains no significance testing. v6 introduces pairwise t-tests comparing ToG-2 with CoK and ToG on WebQSP, Zero-Shot-RE, QALD-10-en, and Creak, reporting p-value thresholds in Table 12. It explains why other comparisons cannot be tested, but adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. Figure 3b reverses the method assignments: at context count 10, v4 assigns 37 to LLM and 34 to BGE-Reranker, while v6 assigns 34 and 37 respectively. New Tables 6 and 9–12 add substantial results on answer sources, efficiency, thresholds, graph completeness, and significance. For example, Table 11 reports 43% EM with full graph retention, 23% with 30% retention, and 29% after adjusting exploration.

T1.justification: Section 4.6 revises the combined-pruning LLM-call bound from 2D + 1 to 2D + (D - 1) + 1. Appendix B.4 explains the additional query-rewriting term. This changes the quantitative cost reasoning; the method equations and other mathematical content remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: tightly coupled KG–text retrieval, deep and faithful reasoning, training-free compatibility with different LLMs, leading performance on six of seven datasets, and improvements for smaller models.

C2.justification: v6 substantially extends the applicability and failure discussion. It explains Creak errors through output-format failures, excessive caution, and annotation mismatch; argues that high pruning thresholds discard potentially useful relations; and discusses why severe graph incompleteness harms reasoning and broader, shallower exploration partially compensates. These extend v4's more general retrieval and evaluation limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a source-code repository link. v6 also specifies the 0.2 relation-pruning cutoff followed by top-W selection, clarifies the relation-pruning ablation, and documents configurations for the new runtime comparison, including CoK's rationale-update setting and NaiveRAG's corpus and BM25/BGE-Reranker pipeline.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same works and substantive positioning relative to text-based, KG-based, and hybrid RAG. Citation-format corrections do not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section structure remain intact. Changes include local grammar and citation formatting, an author-affiliation edit, terminology corrections, and additional appendix subsections. The added scientific material does not entail extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The appendix gains dedicated tables for Creak answer types, total runtime/API calls, pruning thresholds, graph completeness, and significance. Figure 3 is redrawn, including the reversed legend assignments in panel b. Several captions are clarified or corrected, and existing appendix displays are relocated and renumbered; the other original figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v6 provides useful additional scrutiny through incomplete-graph and threshold experiments, Creak failure analysis, and broader runtime comparisons. Figure 3b's revised assignments align the plot with its discussion, while revised call accounting and added implementation information improve clarity. The net gain is limited by the 100-question robustness sample, sparse significance-test documentation, and the unexplained relationship between the temperature revision and unchanged main results.
